question.worked_solution:
To remove the radical $\sqrt{2}$ from the denominator, all we need to do is multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{2}$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4\sqrt{3}}{7\sqrt{2}} & = \\ \frac{4\sqrt{3}}{7\sqrt{2}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} & = \\ \frac{4\sqrt{3}\cdot \sqrt{2}}{7\cdot (\sqrt{2})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{4\sqrt{3}\cdot \sqrt{2}}{7\cdot 2} & = \\ \frac{4\sqrt{3}\cdot \sqrt{2}}{14} & = \\ \frac{2\sqrt{3}\cdot \sqrt{2}}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2\sqrt{3}\cdot \sqrt{2}}{7} & = \\ \frac{2\sqrt{2\cdot 3}}{7} & = \\ \frac{2\sqrt{6}}{7} & \end{aligned}
$$
